title: Count the Islands
statement:
A map is a grid where `1` is land and `0` is water. An **island** is a group of land cells connected **up, down, left or right** (not diagonally).

Return the **number of islands** in the map.
constraints: 1 <= rows, cols <= 50 (every row has the same length)

examples.explanation: Top-left pair, right-side pair, and the single bottom-left cell.
The two land cells only touch diagonally, so they are separate islands.

hints.nudge: When you find a land cell, how can you make sure you never count the rest of its island again?
hints.pattern: Flood fill: BFS or DFS from each unvisited land cell, marking everything it reaches.
hints.walkthrough: Scan the grid. The first time you meet a land cell that is not visited, you have found a new island: add one, then flood-fill from that cell, marking every connected land cell as visited (use a stack or queue; for a 50x50 grid recursion also works). Later cells of the same island are already visited so they are not counted again. Each cell is visited a constant number of times, so O(rows * cols) time.
